name: ftruncate64
description: The ftruncate64() system call truncates the file referenced by the file descriptor to the specified length, supporting large file offsets. If the file is larger, excess data is removed; if shorter, it is extended with null bytes.

parameters.name: fd
parameters.description: File descriptor of the open file to truncate

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: The desired size of the file in bytes

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: fd is not a valid file descriptor
fd is not open for writing, or does not reference a regular file or POSIX shared memory object
The length is larger than the maximum file size
An I/O error occurred updating the inode
The operation was prevented by a file seal or the filesystem does not support extending the file
The file resides on a read-only filesystem
The file is an executable that is being executed
The call was interrupted by a signal handler

bugs: A header file bug in glibc 2.12 meant that the minimum value of _POSIX_C_SOURCE required to expose the declaration of ftruncate() was 200809L instead of 200112L. This has been fixed in later glibc versions.
